**TL;DR**

- **A genuine flight-to-safety AI unwind, not a broad risk-off.** **Nasdaq -2.60%** (steepest drop since June;
- NDX set to erase ~$1T), **S&P 500 -1.21%**, **SOX -6.72%** (biggest since June 23, now ~26% below its June 22 record close), **VIX +14.09%** - but **Russell 2000 +0.11%, Dow ~flat, XLP +3.31%, XLF +1.09%**, and the **10-year yield fell 16bp to ~4.97%**.
- Money went to staples, banks and Treasuries, not to cash. 25 of the 30 names on the board fell.
- **The trigger was capital, not earnings.** Meta beat revenue and guided Q4 up but posted its **first cash outflow in over a decade** and will issue a new class of non-voting shares to fund AI capex (-5.2% to -7.5%).
- Tesla had positive FCF but **cut its 2026 capex forecast**.
- Lam Research's CFO said its $8.6B guide 'would have been a bit higher if not for near-term supply chain constraints' (LRCX -11%, AMAT -7%, ASML -6%).
- Brent hit a five-month high on new Houthi strikes in Saudi. **Investors repriced the cost of the buildout, not its demand.**
- **The single largest move is a record quarter that got sold:
- TTMI -27.67%.** Revenue +60% y/y to a record $1.204B, EPS +118% to $1.46, adj EBITDA margin 20.1% (+400bp) - and the stock lost more than a quarter of its value on **customer-timing noise, $1.7B of capex, acquisition debt and long-lead-time materials**.
- The two most violent single-name prints (TTMI, CRS) were both *good* companies reporting *good* numbers. **A beat is not a floor any more.**

**Top 5 - deep dive (skill hard cap: 5)**

**1. TTMI - -27.67% ($73.89, RVOL 5.93, $7.78B) - **overnight $76.01 (+2.87%)****

**Technology / PCB & AI substrate**

- **Record quarter, record de-rating.** Q3 net sales $1.204B (+60% y/y, record), non-GAAP EPS $1.46 (+118% vs $0.67), adj EBITDA $242.3M at a 20.1% margin (+400bp y/y).
- The market sold the *print* for four things: (1) Data Center & Networking revenue shifted between quarters on **customer scheduling**, so the run rate is not clean;
- (2) **>$1.3B capex already invested or committed plus another $400M planned**; (3) acquisition-related debt with M&A still closing; (4) CCL and T-glass long lead times.
- Beta 2.14, +83% over the prior year, -19% over the prior six months. 52-wk high $223.83

**2. BHVN - +25.02% ($14.69, RVOL 10.07, $2.22B) - **overnight $14.61 (-0.54%)****

**Health Care / Biotech**

- **Two catalysts, both real.** (1) **FDA accepted the resubmitted NDA for Vyglxia (troriluzole) in spinocerebellar ataxia** - a complete response to the Nov 4 2025 action letter, user-fee goal date Q1 2027, adcom to be convened.
- Baird raised its PT $42->$48. (2) **Ono Pharmaceutical Asia licence** for the MoDE IgG degrader portfolio (BHV-1300/1310/1320; BHV-1300 in Phase 3 for Graves'):
- $80M upfront + up to $20M milestones + ~20% royalties - **non-dilutive, and Biohaven keeps US/EU/China**. Against ~$80-85M/quarter of cash burn, the upfront is roughly one extra quarter of runway

**3. FPS - -21.54% ($24.92, RVOL 5.06, $7.95B) - **overnight $25.46 (+2.17%)****

**Industrials / Solar & energy storage**

- **CFO change.** CFO Fiedler stepped down, Amy Ard appointed - the stock fell **below its debut-session low** on it. Morgan Stanley cut its PT $51->$45.
- Options flow confirmed the damage: put volume heavy and directionally bearish, and unusually active option classes opened on Oct 20

**4. CRS - -20.62% ($292.26, RVOL 3.55, $14.48B) - **overnight $294.00 (+0.60%)****

**Materials / Specialty metals**

- **Revenue miss inside an EPS beat.** Q1 FY27 EPS $3.25 beat $3.04, revenue +28% y/y to a record $798.2M but **missed consensus by $32.49M**;
- Specialty Alloys operating income $216.3M was **-6% q/q and missed prior guidance**. CFO said they will 'burn that inventory off'.
- **No free cash flow** - a ~$25M capex burn on brownfield expansion. 32x trailing P/E against 21.5% LT EPS growth = PEG 1.5. Gapped $368.16 -> $330 open.
- Insiders sold 112,996 sh (~$54.6M) in 90 days. **Securities-fraud investigation announced (Frank R. Cruz)**. Consensus still Moderate Buy, $519 PT

**5. MRNA - -17.57% ($202.63, RVOL 2.47, $80.90B) - **overnight $202.11 (-0.26%)****

**Health Care / mRNA vaccines**

- **Embargoed data leaked - and the data was good.** Oncology Central (Informa) prematurely published the embargoed Phase 3 INTerpath-001 data for intismeran autogene (mRNA melanoma vaccine, with Merck's Keytruda).
- Result: **recurrence-or-death risk cut 42%** (vs 49% in Phase 2), **82.2% alive and cancer-free at 2 years vs 70%**, n=1,137, no new safety issues. Trading was halted intraday.
- Bernstein: 'a sell the news event' - the 42% figure fell short of sky-high expectations - Market Perform, $45 PT. Wells Fargo: concerns 'may be overdone'.
- Full presentation **Oct 24 at ESMO, Madrid**. Stock +551% YTD

**Needs human eyes**

- **Tonight's overnight bounce is a short-covering signal, not a fundamental one.** The +1.5% to +4.8% prints cluster in the *most-wounded* names - **AXTI +4.81%, MXL +4.67%, NOK +4.44%, NBIS +2.93%,
- FORM +2.91%, TTMI +2.87%, UCTT +2.77%** - while the non-AI winners went nowhere (BHVN -0.54%, MRNA -0.26%, POOL -0.01%).
- That is the mechanical signature of a bounce off a -6.7% SOX day, not a re-rating.
- **By the twice-tested pattern, expect a weaker regular session today, not a stronger one** - the mirror of yesterday's call.
- **TTMI and CRS both had good quarters and both lost 20-28%.** This is the pattern that matters now:
- the market is no longer rewarding beats, it is penalising capital intensity and guidance. TTMI: $1.7B of capex against a $7.8B company, and Data Center revenue that moved between quarters.
- CRS: zero free cash flow on a $162.5M GAAP profit. **Any remaining 'quality compounder' multiple in AI hardware is the short side now.**
- **MRNA's full data lands Saturday Oct 24 at ESMO.** The leak was *positive* (42% recurrence-risk cut, 82.2% alive and cancer-free at 2 years, n=1,137) and the stock still lost 17.6%.
- Bernstein called it a sell-the-news event and kept Market Perform/$45.
- **If the Saturday presentation adds nothing new, the embargó break has already done the damage - and if it adds something, the reaction to *that* is the trade.** This is the one genuinely binary event on the board and it lands in 36 hours.
- **BHVN is the only genuine positive fundamental on the board, and it did not extend overnight.** FDA acceptance for Vyglxia (Q1 2027 goal date) plus up to $100M of non-dilutive Ono cash against ~$80-85M/quarter of burn.
- It closed +25.02% and is **-0.54% overnight**. The biotech bid was a one-day event; a regulatory acceptance is a step, not an approval, and the adcom is still ahead.
- **FPS is the ugliest tape on the board.** A CFO change with no operational content, a break below the debut-session low, a PT cut, and heavy directionally-bearish put volume.
- Overnight +2.17% is bounce, not a catalyst. **There is no reason in the data to distinguish this from noise.**
- **The macro stack is now actively hostile to long duration.** Brent at a five-month high on Houthi strikes, strong labour data keeping a December Fed hike on the table, a 10-year that fell 16bp to ~4.97% only because of a flight to safety, and **Nov 3 midterms**.
- SOX is -26% from its June peak but still +52.2% YTD against the S&P's +11.8% - **the de-rating is young.**
- **Dates inside the next two weeks:** MRNA full ESMO data **Oct 24**; **SMCI Q1 call Nov 3**; **Fed Oct 27-28**; **Nov 3 midterms**; META and TSLA capex commentary;
- WDC reported after Thursday's close.
